facts.mean: Too tired from too much work.
facts.def: Used when you are worn out after working or studying too long.

example.text: After exams, I felt totally burned out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'burned out' after one busy day.

facts.def: Recovered and able to do normal things again.

example.text: I'm finally back on my feet.

misuse.text: Don't say 'back on my feet' about standing up.
misuse.why: It means healthy and active again.

facts.def: Short for "as soon as possible"; used to ask for something quickly.

example.text: Please send me the notes ASAP.

misuse.text: Don't write 'ASAP' to your boss rudely.

facts.def: A casual word for good, or for agreeing.

example.text: Cool, see you at six!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cool' when someone shares sad news.
misuse.why: It sounds like you don't care.

facts.def: Describes a stingy person; it can also mean low quality.

example.text: He's too cheap to buy lunch.

misuse.text: Don't call grandma 'cheap' for using coupons.

facts.def: To say publicly that someone did something wrong.

example.text: She called me out for being late.

misuse.text: Don't 'call out' a coworker in front of the boss.

facts.def: Wearing fancy clothes to make a good impression.

example.text: He's dressed to impress for the interview.

misuse.text: Don't say 'dressed to impress' about pajamas.
misuse.why: It means a smart, planned outfit.

facts.def: Used when something is very dull.
facts.hook: Two hours of the same slides!

example.text: I was bored stiff in that class.

misuse.text: Don't tell the speaker you're 'bored stiff'.

facts.mean: A day to eat anything you want.
facts.def: A day when you stop a strict diet and enjoy treats.

example.text: Saturday is my cheat day.

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheat day' about exam day.
misuse.why: Cheating on exams breaks the rules.

facts.def: A short, friendly word for a best friend.

example.text: My bestie and I love tacos.

misuse.text: Don't call your new boss your 'bestie'.

facts.def: Used to celebrate a success or good result.

example.text: You passed the test? Big W!

misuse.text: Don't say 'big W' to someone who lost.

facts.def: An opinion that is strong and often unpopular.

example.text: Here's my hot take: pineapple belongs on pizza.

misuse.text: Don't call plain facts a 'hot take'.
misuse.why: It means a bold, debatable opinion.

facts.def: A silly mistake, especially one that is caught on video.
facts.hook: He tripped in the school play!

example.text: That blooper made the whole class laugh.

misuse.text: Don't call a serious mistake a 'blooper'.
misuse.why: It means a small, funny error.

facts.mean: A rough guess of a number.
facts.def: An approximate number, not exact.

example.text: Give me a ballpark figure.

misuse.text: Don't give a 'ballpark figure' for taxes.

facts.def: Used to say you will take part in a plan.

example.text: Game night? Count me in!

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me in' before checking the date.

facts.def: A very good song that gets people moving.

example.text: This new song is a banger!

misuse.text: Don't call a quiet lullaby a 'banger'.
misuse.why: It means an energetic, great song.

facts.def: Used to react when something is awkward, embarrassing or a bad idea.

example.text: Socks with sandals? Big yikes.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host 'big yikes' about dinner.

facts.def: To suddenly forget what you wanted to say or know.
facts.hook: Stage lights on. My mind's empty!

example.text: I blanked out in the middle of my speech.

misuse.text: Don't say 'blank out' about a paper.

facts.mean: Silly online content that feels empty.
facts.def: Jokingly used for low-quality videos you scroll too much.

example.text: Too many videos give me brain rot.

misuse.text: Don't call a documentary 'brain rot'.

facts.def: Used when someone is busy working.

example.text: I'm busy as a bee this week.

misuse.text: Don't say 'busy as a bee' about a lazy afternoon.

facts.def: To wear many layers because it's cold.

example.text: Bundle up, it's freezing outside!

misuse.text: Don't tell a friend to 'bundle up' in summer.
misuse.why: It means put on warm clothes.

facts.def: To come back to a topic after other things.

example.text: Let's circle back to that after lunch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'circle back' when you'll ignore it.
misuse.why: People will wait for your reply.

facts.def: Used to accept someone's point.

example.text: Fair enough, let's try your idea.

misuse.text: Don't say 'fair enough' to a rude insult.
misuse.why: It sounds like you agree with them.

facts.def: Describes things that are corny or too sweet.

example.text: That movie was so cheesy.

misuse.text: Don't call her poem 'cheesy' at the party.
misuse.why: It sounds mean about heartfelt effort.

facts.def: To answer criticism quickly and cleverly.

example.text: She clapped back with a great reply.

misuse.text: Don't 'clap back' at a parent's advice.

facts.def: Slang for cool clothes and a stylish look.
facts.hook: New jacket, new shoes, new confidence!

example.text: Nice jacket, you've got drip today.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'nice drip' at work.
misuse.why: It's too slangy for formal settings.

facts.def: Used when something small has let you down.

example.text: I'm bummed out about the trip.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummed out' about serious loss.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

facts.def: Said to show something is perfect, like a great meal.

example.text: The soup was chef's kiss.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chef's kiss' about burnt toast.

facts.mean: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.def: Casual slang used for a friend or buddy.

example.text: Thanks, bro, you saved me!

misuse.text: Don't call your grandma 'bro'.

facts.def: To lead a team to victory with great skill.

example.text: Mia carried us in the final round.

misuse.text: Don't say 'she carried us' about a lazy teammate.
misuse.why: It praises someone who did the work.

facts.def: Used after a joke to show you didn't mean it.

example.text: I ate your cake! Just kidding.

misuse.text: Don't say 'just kidding' after a serious insult.

facts.mean: I'm in trouble or out of luck.
facts.def: Used jokingly when a situation looks bad for you.

example.text: I forgot my notes. I'm cooked.

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm cooked' when you merely feel sleepy.
misuse.why: It means you're in real trouble.

facts.mean: Fancy, and a bit too proud.
facts.def: Liking expensive or fancy things, sometimes in a showy way.

example.text: This coffee shop is so bougie.

misuse.text: Don't call your host 'bougie' at dinner.
misuse.why: It can sound snobbish and rude.

facts.def: Used to politely say you won't join a plan.
facts.hook: Wanna go to the late show?

example.text: I'm tired, so count me out.

misuse.text: Don't say 'count me out' to your boss's request.
misuse.why: It sounds like a flat refusal.

facts.def: Someone who behaves with style and kindness.

example.text: Our coach is a real class act.

misuse.text: Don't say 'class act' about a school class.

facts.def: A short reaction to something silly or unbelievable.

example.text: Bruh, you forgot your homework again?

misuse.text: Don't say 'bruh' to your boss.

facts.def: To keep working late into the night.

example.text: We burned the midnight oil last night.

misuse.text: Don't say it about lighting candles.

facts.mean: A title that tricks you to click.
facts.def: A catchy headline that isn't worth reading.

example.text: That title is pure clickbait.

misuse.text: Don't call a real news story 'clickbait'.

facts.def: To decide to finish work or an activity for now.

example.text: We're tired, let's call it a day.

misuse.text: Don't 'call it a day' before the deadline.

facts.def: To begin to feel ill with something like a cold.

example.text: I think I'm coming down with a cold.

misuse.text: Don't say you 'came down with' a gift.
misuse.why: It means starting to get sick.

facts.def: Short for "for your information"; used to share a helpful fact.

example.text: FYI, the shop closes at five.

misuse.text: Don't use 'FYI' to scold someone.
misuse.why: It can sound cold and sharp.

facts.def: Used to say you accept an idea.

example.text: Pizza or tacos? Fine by me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'fine by me' when you're upset.
misuse.why: People will think you truly don't mind.

facts.def: Describes jokes that are so silly they're embarrassing.

example.text: Dad's jokes are so corny.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher's joke 'corny' out loud.

facts.mean: Fuss and arguments about small things.
facts.def: Needless trouble or arguments between people.

example.text: I don't want any drama this year.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's real problem 'drama'.
misuse.why: It makes serious feelings sound silly.

facts.def: A moment to show your outfit and get opinions.

example.text: Quick fit check before school!

misuse.text: Don't ask for a 'fit check' at the gym.

facts.def: Used to tell someone to feel better.

example.text: Cheer up, we're having pizza!

misuse.text: Don't say 'cheer up' to someone grieving.
misuse.why: It sounds like you dismiss their pain.

facts.mean: Food that makes you feel better.
facts.def: Simple food that makes you feel better and at home.

example.text: Warm soup is my comfort food.

misuse.text: Don't call hospital food your 'comfort food'.
misuse.why: It means food that cozily soothes you.

facts.def: A friendly word for a friend.
facts.hook: Who studies with you every night?

example.text: He's my study buddy.

misuse.text: Don't say 'buddy' to an angry stranger.

facts.def: Used when someone does well at an important time.

example.text: That last-minute goal was so clutch.

misuse.text: Don't say 'clutch' about a small purse.
misuse.why: Here it means great under pressure.

facts.def: Short for legitimate; used for things that are real, true or really good.

example.text: This shop is legit, my sister bought shoes there.

misuse.text: Don't say 'legit' in a legal document.

facts.def: To ask someone to be less strict or critical.

example.text: Cut me some slack, I'm new.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'cut me some slack' daily.

facts.def: To cost so much that you can't afford it.

example.text: Don't worry, this lunch won't break the bank.

misuse.text: Don't say 'break the bank' at a bank.
misuse.why: It only means costing too much.

facts.def: To visit someone casually, often without a plan.

example.text: Feel free to drop by anytime.

misuse.text: Don't 'drop by' a stranger's house unannounced.
misuse.why: Even casual visits need a welcome.

facts.def: Used when someone is doing really well at something.

example.text: You're crushing it at your new job!

misuse.text: Don't tell a struggling friend 'crushing it' sarcastically.

facts.def: Used when something is a bit sad or disappointing.

example.text: The trip is canceled? What a bummer.

misuse.text: Don't say 'bummer' to someone who lost a loved one.
misuse.why: It's too light for deep grief.

facts.def: To study many things quickly just before a test.

example.text: I must cram for math.

misuse.text: Don't 'cram' for a three-year course.
misuse.why: Cramming only works for short tests.

facts.mean: Scroll bad news for too long.
facts.def: To keep reading sad online news without stopping.

example.text: Stop doomscrolling and go to sleep.

misuse.text: Don't say 'doomscroll' about reading a recipe.

facts.def: A casual way to say you will sleep.

example.text: I'm going to catch some Zs.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss you'll 'catch some Zs'.
misuse.why: It sounds like napping on work time.

facts.def: Used when something or someone is completely fixed or healthy.

example.text: After a nap, I feel good as new.

misuse.text: Don't call a broken phone 'good as new'.
misuse.why: It means fully repaired or healed.

facts.def: To begin a project or process.

example.text: Let's get the ball rolling with ideas.

misuse.text: Don't say 'get the ball rolling' about finishing.

facts.def: Used to agree strongly.

example.text: Pizza tonight? For sure!

misuse.text: Don't say 'for sure' if you might cancel.
misuse.why: It sounds like a firm promise.

facts.def: Used for things that are dull or not cool.

example.text: That party was kind of lame.

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's idea 'lame' in front of everyone.

facts.mean: A friend who is also a rival.
facts.def: Someone who acts friendly but competes with you.

example.text: She's my frenemy, always competing with me.

misuse.text: Don't call your best friend your 'frenemy'.
misuse.why: It suggests you secretly dislike her.

facts.def: Used to say that something reminds you of a style or mood.
facts.hook: That coat looks like old movies!

example.text: That coat is giving old movie star.

misuse.text: Don't say 'it's giving' to a job interviewer.

facts.def: Used to encourage someone who is sad.

example.text: Chin up, tomorrow will be better.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chin up' to someone crying hard.

facts.def: Used to invite people to begin eating.

example.text: Dinner is ready, so dig in!

misuse.text: Don't tell guests to 'dig in' before the host.
misuse.why: Formal dinners wait for the host.

facts.def: A friendly, casual goodbye.

example.text: Catch you later, I have to go!

misuse.text: Don't end a formal interview with 'catch you later'.
misuse.why: It's too casual for formal talks.

facts.def: A big, impressive win.

example.text: We scored in the last second. Epic win!

misuse.text: Don't say 'epic win' about a tiny task.

facts.def: Short for "not gonna lie", before an honest opinion.

example.text: Ngl, I loved that movie.

misuse.text: Don't use 'ngl' in a job application.

facts.def: A mistake or failure that is so big it is almost funny.

example.text: My cake fell flat. Total epic fail!

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's loss an 'epic fail'.

facts.mean: Give a bit of money to share.
facts.def: To give some money so a group can buy something.

example.text: Let's all chip in for her gift.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chip in' about potato chips.

facts.mean: The plan for what to do.
facts.def: A clear plan to reach a goal.
facts.hook: Test tomorrow. Where do we start?

example.text: So, what's the game plan?

misuse.text: Don't call a vague idea a 'game plan'.

facts.def: Slang for something excellent or stylish.

example.text: Those sneakers are fire!

misuse.text: Don't yell 'fire' in a crowded room.

facts.def: A casual way to ask someone to repeat.

example.text: Come again? It's too loud here.

misuse.text: Don't say 'come again' when you heard clearly.

facts.def: To begin studying hard.

example.text: I have to hit the books tonight.

misuse.text: Don't tell your friend to 'hit the books' at a party.

facts.def: People who love the same show or band.

example.text: The fandom loves this band.

misuse.text: Don't call your coworkers a 'fandom'.
misuse.why: It means devoted fans of one thing.

facts.def: Used when you are so tired you can barely move.

example.text: I'm dog tired after that long hike.

misuse.text: Don't call your pet 'dog tired' literally.

facts.def: An idiom for very heavy rain.

example.text: It's raining cats and dogs!

misuse.text: Don't look for real animals when it's 'raining cats and dogs'.
misuse.why: It's an idiom for heavy rain.

facts.def: Early information so someone can be ready.

example.text: Just a heads up, the meeting starts early.

misuse.text: Don't say 'heads up' after the problem happens.

facts.def: Used to say you agree to a plan or want to do it.

example.text: We're going bowling tonight. Are you down?

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm down' when you feel sad.
misuse.why: It can also mean feeling low.

facts.def: Used when something doesn't seem logical.

example.text: This game rule makes no sense.

misuse.text: Don't say 'makes no sense' about your boss's plan.

facts.def: Something unfair said to hurt someone.

example.text: That joke was a low blow.

misuse.text: Don't call fair criticism a 'low blow'.
misuse.why: It may just be honest feedback.

facts.mean: Succeed at wearing or doing something bold.
facts.def: To manage something hard or bold, like a style.

example.text: Not everyone can pull off that color.

misuse.text: Don't say 'pull off' when you mean 'remove'.

facts.mean: Grumpy and in a bad mood.
facts.def: Describes someone tired or annoyed.

example.text: I'm cranky before breakfast.

misuse.text: Don't call your boss 'cranky' in an email.

facts.mean: A person who loves good food.
facts.def: Someone who enjoys trying and talking about food.
facts.hook: She reviews every restaurant in town!

example.text: My sister is a total foodie.

misuse.text: Don't call a chef a 'foodie'.
misuse.why: A chef cooks; a foodie loves eating.

facts.def: A British way to say thank you or goodbye.
facts.hook: He held the door. Say thanks!

example.text: Cheers for the lift!

misuse.text: Don't expect Americans to understand 'cheers' as thanks.

facts.def: Said politely after a match ends.

example.text: GG, that was a fun match!

misuse.text: Don't type 'GG' to your boss after a project.

facts.def: A hand-on-face gesture of disbelief.

example.text: My phone was in my hand. Facepalm!

misuse.text: Don't 'facepalm' at your teacher's answer.

facts.def: Used when you have almost no money at all.

example.text: I'm flat broke until Friday.

misuse.text: Don't say 'flat broke' about a broken phone.

facts.def: To contact someone by text or call.

example.text: Hit me up if you need help.

misuse.text: Don't say 'hit me up' to your professor.

facts.mean: A big change for the better.
facts.def: A big improvement in how someone looks, feels or lives.

example.text: Wow, your glow-up this year is amazing.

misuse.text: Don't tell someone their glow-up means they looked bad.
misuse.why: It implies they looked bad before.

facts.def: Used when something is so funny you can't stop laughing.

example.text: We were cracking up at his joke.

misuse.text: Don't say 'cracking up' about a cracked phone.

facts.def: Used when something is too confusing to understand.

example.text: This homework is all Greek to me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'it's all Greek to me' about easy tasks.

facts.mean: Show off something you're proud of.
facts.def: To show off what you have or can do.

example.text: He keeps flexing his new sneakers online.

misuse.text: Don't 'flex' your salary at a job interview.

facts.mean: A person who wakes up early.
facts.def: Someone who likes to get up and start early.

example.text: My dad is an early bird.

misuse.text: Don't call a late sleeper an 'early bird'.
misuse.why: It means someone who wakes early.

facts.def: A day with extremely hot weather.

example.text: Today is a real scorcher!

misuse.text: Don't say 'scorcher' about a cold morning.
misuse.why: It means a very hot day.

facts.def: Being included and informed about what's going on.

example.text: Keep me in the loop about the trip.

misuse.text: Don't say 'in the loop' about a roller coaster.
misuse.why: It means knowing the latest news.

facts.def: A polite way to say no or that you're okay.

example.text: No thanks, I'm good.

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm good' if you want more food.

facts.def: Used to show you aren't impressed.

example.text: The movie? Meh.

misuse.text: Don't say 'meh' about a friend's cooking.

facts.def: Used for someone who makes a big deal out of small things.

example.text: Counting every cookie is petty, don't you think?

misuse.text: Don't call a real complaint 'petty'.

facts.def: To look great in something or do well.

example.text: You totally rock it in that hat!

misuse.text: Don't say 'rock it' about an actual rock.

facts.def: Short for delusional; used playfully about big dreams.

example.text: I'm delulu, I think he'll text first.

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's real goal 'delulu'.
misuse.why: It mocks hopes that could come true.

facts.def: To eat something small and quick.

example.text: Want to grab a bite after class?

misuse.text: Don't say 'grab a bite' before a seven-course dinner.
misuse.why: It means a quick, light meal.

facts.def: To relax and do nothing special; also used to say someone is easygoing.

example.text: I'm just going to chill at home today.

misuse.text: Don't say 'chill' when someone needs urgent help.
misuse.why: It sounds like you don't care.

facts.mean: Work hard for a long time.
facts.def: To keep working at something to improve or earn.

example.text: I'm grinding to reach level fifty.

misuse.text: Don't call your boss's meeting 'the grind' aloud.
misuse.why: It sounds like you hate work.

facts.def: Used when you don't know something at all.

example.text: I have no clue what to cook.

misuse.text: Don't say 'no clue' in a job interview.

facts.def: A quick, casual way to say sorry.

example.text: My bad, I forgot your book.

misuse.text: Don't say 'my bad' after a serious accident.
misuse.why: It's too light for real harm.

facts.def: Used when something costs far less than it should.

example.text: Ten dollars? It's a steal!

misuse.text: Don't say 'it's a steal' about actual theft.
misuse.why: It means a great low price.

facts.mean: Done very late, close to the time.
facts.def: Describes something decided just before it happens.

example.text: It was a last minute decision.

misuse.text: Don't send a 'last minute' invite to your boss.

facts.def: A word for the best person in their field; it stands for greatest of all time.

example.text: My grandma is the GOAT of soup.

misuse.text: Don't say 'GOAT' while pointing at a farm animal.
misuse.why: It means greatest ever, not the animal.

facts.def: Used for something so awkward or embarrassing it's hard to watch.

example.text: My old school photos are so cringe.

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's heartfelt gift 'cringe'.

facts.def: Used when you are totally focused on a task.

example.text: I'm locked in until this essay is done.

misuse.text: Don't say you're 'locked in' while scrolling.

facts.def: Strong excitement from many people.

example.text: Is the movie worth the hype?

misuse.text: Don't call a quiet event 'hype'.

facts.def: A casual way to say you are going to sleep.

example.text: I'm tired, so I'm going to hit the sack.

misuse.text: Don't say 'hit the sack' at a formal dinner.
misuse.why: It's casual for going to bed.

facts.def: Used when you are very sweaty from heat or effort.

example.text: I'm sweating buckets after that run.

misuse.text: Don't say 'sweating buckets' about a calm interview.

facts.def: A way to ask someone to share new information.

example.text: Keep me posted on the test results!

misuse.text: Don't say 'keep me posted' if you ignore updates.

facts.def: A short way to say you agree to join.

example.text: Pizza night? I'm in!

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm in' before knowing the price.
misuse.why: It sounds like a firm yes.

facts.def: Used to say that something is only okay, not special.

example.text: The movie was mid, honestly.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss the meeting was 'mid'.

facts.def: A sign that something might be a problem.
facts.hook: He lied twice on date one!

example.text: That sudden price change is a red flag.

misuse.text: Don't say 'red flag' about a friend's haircut.
misuse.why: It's for warning signs, not taste.

facts.def: Shopping for used items in cheap shops.

example.text: We're thrifting for jackets this weekend.

misuse.text: Don't say you're 'thrifting' at a luxury boutique.

facts.def: Used when something bothers you a lot.

example.text: That noise drives me up the wall.

misuse.text: Don't tell your teacher she 'drives you up the wall'.

facts.def: A mix of hungry and angry, for when hunger ruins your mood.

example.text: Feed me, I'm hangry!

misuse.text: Don't say you're 'hangry' at a job interview.

facts.def: Describes someone who wants too much attention.
facts.hook: She texts me every five minutes!

example.text: My puppy is so clingy.

misuse.text: Don't call a friend 'clingy' to her face.

facts.def: A delay between what you do and what happens on screen.

example.text: There's too much lag, I can't play.

misuse.text: Don't say 'lag' about a person's slow walking.
misuse.why: It describes slow connections, not people.

facts.mean: I don't want to upset you.
facts.def: Used before an honest comment that might sound harsh.

example.text: No offense, but I prefer the red one.

misuse.text: Don't say 'no offense' before a harsh insult.

facts.def: A simple way to admit a mistake.

example.text: That's my fault, I'm sorry.

misuse.text: Don't say 'my fault' if it wasn't yours.

facts.def: Used to say you will pay for the others.

example.text: Don't worry, it's my treat tonight.

misuse.text: Don't say 'my treat' if you can't pay.
misuse.why: Everyone expects you to cover it.

facts.def: Used to say it's time to start or leave.

example.text: Backpacks on, let's roll!

misuse.text: Don't say 'let's roll' to start a serious meeting.

facts.def: Describes something so famous or stylish that people remember it forever.

example.text: That red jacket is truly iconic.

misuse.text: Don't call your lunch 'iconic' in a report.

facts.def: A playful way to say something is very simple.

example.text: Making toast is easy peasy.

misuse.text: Don't say 'easy peasy' about a friend's hard task.
misuse.why: It makes their struggle look small.

facts.mean: Too hard for me to understand.
facts.def: Used when something is too complex.

example.text: That lesson went over my head.

misuse.text: Don't say 'over my head' about a hat.
misuse.why: It means too hard to understand.

facts.def: Short for "I don't know" in texts.

example.text: IDK, maybe we should stay home.

misuse.text: Don't write 'IDK' to your boss's question.

facts.def: Used to say you are extremely tired, usually after a long day.

example.text: I'm beat, so I'm skipping dinner tonight.

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm beat' after winning a game.

facts.def: Used when you feel slightly ill or not well.
facts.hook: Why do I feel off today?

example.text: I'm a bit under the weather.

misuse.text: Don't say 'under the weather' about a storm.
misuse.why: It means feeling a little sick.

facts.def: Used to say you can't take more work.
facts.hook: Can you take one more task?

example.text: Sorry, my plate is full.

misuse.text: Don't say 'my plate is full' at dinner.
misuse.why: It means too many tasks, not food.

facts.def: Used when the best choice is obvious and needs no thought.

example.text: Free tickets? It's a no-brainer!

misuse.text: Don't call a hard decision 'a no-brainer'.
misuse.why: It dismisses the other person's worries.

facts.mean: Not as good as people say.
facts.def: Used for something that gets more praise than it deserves.

example.text: I think that cafe is overrated.

misuse.text: Don't call her favorite band 'overrated' at her party.

facts.def: To share juicy news about other people.

example.text: Spill the tea about the school trip!

misuse.text: Don't ask your teacher to 'spill the tea'.

facts.mean: I'm in this phase of life.
facts.def: Used playfully for a current phase or interest.

example.text: I'm in my baking era right now.

misuse.text: Don't say 'my era' about a history class.
misuse.why: It means a personal life phase.

facts.def: Used when food or drink is perfectly satisfying.

example.text: That soup really hit the spot.

misuse.text: Don't say 'hit the spot' about a bruise.

facts.mean: A casual word for a person.
facts.def: Used to call a friend or show surprise.

example.text: Dude, you're not going to believe this!

misuse.text: Don't call your principal 'dude'.

facts.def: To grow in skill, like moving up in a game.
facts.hook: Time to get better at cooking!

example.text: I want to level up my cooking.

misuse.text: Don't tell your teacher to 'level up'.
misuse.why: It sounds like a challenge, not respect.

facts.def: Used when an offer comes with no hidden rules.

example.text: It's a free gift, no strings attached.

misuse.text: Don't say 'no strings attached' about a guitar.
misuse.why: It means free, with no conditions.

facts.def: Used to say that something is not serious.

example.text: It's no big deal, really.

misuse.text: Don't say 'no big deal' when it hurt you.

facts.def: Used when a restaurant gives you something for free.

example.text: Dessert is on the house today!

misuse.text: Don't say 'on the house' about a real house.
misuse.why: It means free from the business.

facts.def: Used to say there is no hurry.

example.text: No rush, send it tomorrow.

misuse.text: Don't say 'no rush' if it's urgent.

facts.def: Used to praise someone who did something great.

example.text: Thanks for the snacks, you're a legend!

misuse.text: Don't call your boss a 'legend' sarcastically.
misuse.why: People may not know it's a joke.

facts.def: Used for someone who is dramatic or over the top for small things.
facts.hook: She brought balloons to study group!

example.text: She brought balloons to study group. So extra.

misuse.text: Don't call your boss's effort 'extra'.
misuse.why: It sounds like you mock them.

facts.def: Used for something that is very easy to do.

example.text: The quiz was a piece of cake.

misuse.text: Don't call a hard exam 'a piece of cake'.
misuse.why: It means easy, so you'll sound arrogant.

facts.mean: A person with many online followers.
facts.def: Someone who shapes what others buy or like online.

example.text: My cousin wants to be an influencer.

misuse.text: Don't call a doctor an 'influencer'.
misuse.why: It means online fame, not expertise.

facts.mean: I have too much to do.
facts.def: Used to say you are extremely busy with work or tasks.

example.text: Sorry, I'm swamped with homework.

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm swamped' when you're bored.
misuse.why: It means too much to do.

facts.def: To make quick contact with someone about a topic.

example.text: Let's touch base on Monday about the plan.

misuse.text: Don't say 'touch base' about baseball.

facts.def: Used when people share the same understanding.

example.text: Let's make sure we're on the same page.

misuse.text: Don't say 'on the same page' about a paperback.
misuse.why: It means shared understanding, not books.

facts.def: Describes things that look cheap or show poor taste.

example.text: That sign looks a bit tacky.

misuse.text: Don't call your host's decor 'tacky'.
misuse.why: It insults their taste in their own home.

facts.def: To insult someone in a sneaky, indirect way.
facts.hook: She smiled, then insulted my hat!

example.text: She threw shade at my new hat.

misuse.text: Don't say 'throw shade' about a tree's shadow.

facts.def: Used when you've had enough of a problem.

example.text: I'm fed up with this rain.

misuse.text: Don't tell your host you're 'fed up' with dinner.
misuse.why: It sounds like you hate the food.

facts.def: Used to say you are very hungry. It's an exaggeration.

example.text: I'm starving! What's for dinner?

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm starving' to people facing real hunger.
misuse.why: It's an exaggeration and can sound insensitive.

facts.def: Short for family; a friendly way to call close friends.

example.text: What's up, fam?

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher 'fam' in class.

facts.mean: A beginner who is still learning.
facts.def: A person new to a game or skill.

example.text: I'm a noob, so please be patient.

misuse.text: Don't call a new coworker a 'noob'.

facts.def: Said when you share information that shouldn't be repeated.

example.text: Off the record, I like the red one.

misuse.text: Don't repeat what was said 'off the record'.
misuse.why: It was shared as a secret.

facts.def: A friendly way to say something isn't a problem.

example.text: No worries, it's only a small spot.

quiz.ask: "No worries" is a way to say…

misuse.text: Don't say 'no worries' if you're truly upset.

facts.mean: A person who saves every cent.
facts.def: Someone who is very careful with money.

example.text: My dad is a penny-pincher.

misuse.text: Don't call a family friend a 'penny-pincher'.

facts.def: Used when you are unsure which option to choose.

example.text: I'm on the fence about the trip.

misuse.text: Don't say 'on the fence' about a real fence.

facts.def: The confident feeling of someone who acts like the hero of their own story.
facts.hook: She walks in like a star!

example.text: She entered with main character energy.

misuse.text: Don't say 'main character energy' about yourself at work.

facts.def: Used to ask or say that something is true.

example.text: You won a ticket? For real?

misuse.text: Don't say 'for real' to doubt a friend's pain.
misuse.why: It sounds like you don't believe them.

facts.def: A short test the teacher gives without warning.

example.text: We had a pop quiz in math today.

misuse.text: Don't call a planned exam a 'pop quiz'.

facts.def: Short for "in real life", used to compare with online.

example.text: I met her IRL last week.

misuse.text: Don't use 'IRL' in a formal letter.

facts.mean: A person who stays up late.
facts.def: Someone who likes being awake at night.

example.text: I'm a night owl, so I study late.

misuse.text: Don't call a morning person a 'night owl'.
misuse.why: It means someone who stays up late.

facts.def: To finish a task, meeting or talk.

example.text: Let's wrap up and go home.

misuse.text: Don't say 'wrap up' in the middle of a talk.

facts.def: Used to end a point with confidence.

example.text: Pizza is the best food, period.

misuse.text: Don't write 'periodt' in a school essay.
misuse.why: It's texting slang, not formal writing.

facts.mean: Someone who tries way too hard.
facts.def: A person who works very hard to impress.

example.text: Don't be a tryhard, just relax.

misuse.text: Don't call your teammate a 'tryhard' for training.

facts.def: Describes people or places that make you feel bad.
facts.hook: Why does that chat feel awful?

example.text: That group chat feels toxic.

misuse.text: Don't call spicy soup 'toxic' at dinner.
misuse.why: It means harmful, not just strong.

facts.def: The worry that others are having fun or doing something great without you.
facts.hook: Everyone's at the party except me!

example.text: I have serious FOMO when I see party photos.

misuse.text: Don't say 'FOMO' about a fear of spiders.

facts.def: To end contact with a person without any explanation.

example.text: He ghosted our group chat last week.

misuse.text: Don't say 'ghosted' about a friend who's sick.

facts.def: A person who seems to follow a routine with no thought.
facts.hook: She repeats the same line daily!

example.text: I feel like an NPC doing chores.

misuse.text: Don't call your real friend an 'NPC'.
misuse.why: It says they have no personality.

facts.mean: Looks like you can't trust it.
facts.def: Used for people, places or websites that seem a bit unsafe or fake.

example.text: That website looks sketchy, so I'm closing it.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's cooking 'sketchy' to her.
misuse.why: It sounds like you distrust it.

facts.def: To make a small error.

example.text: I slipped up and forgot the key.

misuse.text: Don't call a huge disaster a 'slip up'.

facts.mean: Spend more than usual on fun.
facts.def: To spend more money on a treat than you normally would.

example.text: I splurged on a nice dinner.

misuse.text: Don't say 'splurge' about a tiny snack.
misuse.why: It means spending lots, not little.

facts.def: To decide what to do as things happen.

example.text: Let's play it by ear.

misuse.text: Don't say 'play it by ear' for a big wedding.

facts.def: Used when you did something exactly right.
facts.hook: My speech got a standing ovation!

example.text: I nailed it! The teacher clapped.

misuse.text: Don't say 'nailed it' after you failed.

facts.def: Used for something that makes you laugh a lot.

example.text: That joke was hilarious!

misuse.text: Don't say 'hilarious' about someone's real accident.

facts.def: To stay awake all night to finish work or study.

example.text: I pulled an all-nighter for science.

misuse.text: Don't say you 'pulled an all-nighter' if you slept.
misuse.why: It means no sleep at all.

facts.def: When someone sees your message but doesn't reply.

example.text: I got left on read again.

misuse.text: Don't say 'left on read' about a book.
misuse.why: It means no reply after reading.

facts.def: Used when you are almost out of energy.

example.ctx: At the end of a hike
example.text: I'm on my last legs after this hike.

misuse.text: Don't say 'on my last legs' about a chair.

facts.def: A short way to say you feel or do the same.

example.text: Tired already? Same.

misuse.text: Don't say 'same' to someone who is grieving.
misuse.why: It sounds careless without real comfort.

facts.def: Used when something or someone bothers you.

example.text: His loud humming gets on my nerves.

misuse.text: Don't tell your teacher she 'gets on your nerves'.

facts.def: To spend free time with someone without a special plan.

example.text: Do you want to hang out this weekend?

misuse.text: Don't invite your boss to 'hang out' formally.
misuse.why: It sounds too casual for work.

facts.def: Short for overpowered; used when something is unfairly strong.
facts.hook: That sword beats every other one!

example.text: That new sword is totally OP.

misuse.text: Don't call a fair rule 'OP' in class.
misuse.why: It means unfairly strong in games.

facts.def: Used to say that someone is lying or exaggerating.

example.ctx: Chatting with a friend at school
example.text: You ran a marathon yesterday? That's cap.

misuse.text: Don't tell your teacher 'that's cap'.
misuse.why: It calls someone a liar rudely.

facts.def: Used when you have little money to spend right now.

example.text: I'm tight on cash this month.

misuse.text: Don't say 'tight on cash' about a tight shirt.

facts.def: A polite way to say no now and yes later.

example.text: Can I take a rain check? I have homework.

misuse.text: Don't ask for a 'rain check' after canceling thrice.
misuse.why: It sounds like an empty excuse.

facts.def: Used for something that is perfectly done or stylish.
facts.hook: Did I pick the right outfit?

example.text: Your hair is on point today.

misuse.text: Don't say 'on point' about a sharp pencil.
misuse.why: It means perfect and exactly right.

facts.mean: A person or thing in chaos.
facts.def: Used for someone or something very messy.

example.text: Today I'm a total hot mess.

misuse.text: Don't call your boss a 'hot mess'.

facts.def: To miss a class on purpose.

example.text: Don't skip class, the quiz is today.

misuse.text: Don't tell your teacher you plan to 'skip class'.

facts.def: To read posts in a group without joining in.
facts.hook: I read everything but never post!

example.text: I just lurk in that group chat.

misuse.text: Don't tell your friend 'I lurk on your profile'.

facts.def: To become too tired to continue.

example.text: I ran out of steam around noon.

misuse.text: Don't say 'run out of steam' about a kettle.

facts.mean: Got it, no need to explain.
facts.def: Used to say you agree and need no more details.

example.text: Free snacks? Say less!

misuse.text: Don't say 'say less' when you need details.
misuse.why: It tells them to stop explaining.

facts.def: Used to tell someone to stop being upset.

example.text: Come on, get over it!

misuse.text: Don't tell a sad friend to 'get over it'.

facts.def: Used before a short version of a long story.
facts.hook: Don't ask why my bike broke!

example.text: Long story short, my bike broke.

misuse.text: Don't say it, then tell a very long story.
misuse.why: It promises you'll keep it brief.

facts.def: To stop playing suddenly because you are upset.

example.text: He rage quit after he lost.

misuse.text: Don't 'rage quit' a team meeting online.
misuse.why: It leaves colleagues confused and annoyed.

facts.def: Used for something that is authentic and good.

example.text: This shop is the real deal.

misuse.text: Don't call a cheap copy 'the real deal'.
misuse.why: It means genuine and truly great.

facts.mean: Good for the price or effort.
facts.def: Used when something deserves its cost or hard work.
facts.hook: Two hours in line. Still good?

example.text: Long line, but worth it.

misuse.text: Don't say 'worth it' about a terrible trip.
misuse.why: It means the result was good.

facts.def: Used to agree to someone's suggestion.

example.text: Pizza, then movie? Sounds like a plan!

misuse.text: Don't say 'sounds like a plan' about a messy idea.
misuse.why: It means a clear, agreed plan.

facts.def: To do something extremely well or look amazing doing it.
facts.hook: She just gave the best speech!

example.text: You slayed that speech!

misuse.text: Don't say 'slay' in a serious meeting.

facts.mean: I'm so overwhelmed I can't speak.
facts.def: Used when something is too funny, cute or shocking.

example.text: That puppy video? I can't even!

misuse.text: Don't say 'I can't even' in a formal speech.

facts.def: A student who gets special favor from the teacher.
facts.hook: She always sits front, always smiles!

example.text: Sam is the teacher's pet.

misuse.text: Don't call a classmate 'teacher's pet' to her face.

facts.mean: A funny image or joke online.
facts.def: A popular joke or image shared online.

example.text: She sent me a funny meme.

misuse.text: Don't send a 'meme' to a serious client.

facts.def: Used when you keep going even though you are almost empty of energy.

example.text: I'm running on fumes after finals week.

misuse.text: Don't say 'running on fumes' when fully rested.

facts.def: Used to agree or strongly say something.

example.text: That pizza was totally worth it.

misuse.text: Don't say 'totally' if you partly disagree.

facts.def: Used to keep a mood happy and kind.

example.text: Beach day, good vibes only!

misuse.text: Don't say 'good vibes only' to someone sharing worries.
misuse.why: It tells them to hide feelings.

facts.def: A casual word for a friend.

example.text: Cheers, mate, see you tomorrow!

misuse.text: Don't call every American stranger 'mate'.

facts.def: Short for suspicious; used when something or someone seems odd.

example.text: You were near the cookies. Kind of sus.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher 'sus' in class.

facts.def: Used before saying your real opinion.

example.text: To be honest, I liked the first one.

misuse.text: Don't say 'to be honest' before every sentence.
misuse.why: It makes other sentences sound untrue.

facts.def: To stop by a place quickly.

example.text: I'll swing by after school.

misuse.text: Don't say 'swing by' for a two-day visit.

facts.def: Used for work or results that are really great.

example.text: You did a stellar job today.

misuse.text: Don't call a so-so job 'stellar'.

facts.def: On social media, it means a post got more replies than likes.

example.text: His post got ratioed by replies.

misuse.text: Don't say 'ratio'd' about math homework.
misuse.why: It means more replies than likes.

facts.def: Used when you feel totally exhausted.

example.text: I'm wiped out, so no movie tonight.

misuse.text: Don't say 'wiped out' about cleaning a table.

facts.def: Describes a deal that helps both sides.

example.text: It's a win-win for both of us.

misuse.text: Don't call a one-sided deal a 'win-win'.

facts.def: Used to encourage someone during a hard time.

example.text: Hang in there, almost the weekend!

misuse.text: Don't say 'hang in there' about hanging laundry.
misuse.why: It means keep going through hard times.

facts.def: When someone's words and actions don't match.
facts.hook: He likes me? He ignores me?

example.text: He sends mixed signals about the trip.

misuse.text: Don't call clear instructions 'mixed signals'.

facts.def: To admit a loss or defeat.

example.text: You lost, so just take the L.

misuse.text: Don't tell a sad friend to 'take the L'.
misuse.why: It sounds like you mock them.

facts.mean: A view most people disagree with.
facts.def: An opinion many people may not share.

example.text: Unpopular opinion: Mondays are fine.

misuse.text: Don't post 'unpopular opinion' about something everyone likes.

facts.def: To go with a group that didn't invite you directly.

example.text: Can I tag along to the movie?

misuse.text: Don't 'tag along' on someone's private date.

facts.def: Used about music or food that is excellent.

example.text: Turn it up! This new song really slaps.

misuse.text: Don't say 'that slaps' about a school lecture.

facts.def: Used when something makes you laugh a lot.

example.text: That meme? I'm weak!

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm weak' when you're really ill.
misuse.why: People may think you are unwell.

facts.def: Short for "shaking my head", showing disapproval.

example.text: He forgot again, SMH.

misuse.text: Don't write 'SMH' in a work report.

facts.def: Used when you're so tired you could fall asleep.

example.text: I'm zonked, so I'm going to bed.

misuse.text: Don't say 'zonked' in a business email.

facts.def: Used to agree to a plan.

example.text: Seven o'clock works for me.

misuse.text: Don't say 'works for me' if the time's bad.
misuse.why: People will plan around your yes.

facts.mean: Really, and I'm not hiding it.
facts.def: Used to say something strongly and openly. It's the opposite of lowkey.

example.text: I highkey love this new album.

misuse.text: Don't say 'highkey' in a formal presentation.

facts.def: A polite way to answer thanks.

example.text: Thanks! My pleasure.

misuse.text: Don't say 'my pleasure' when you're annoyed.

facts.def: Used when plans are still uncertain.

example.text: Our trip is still up in the air.

misuse.text: Don't say 'up in the air' about a flight.

facts.def: Used for something excellent.

example.text: The service here is top-notch.

misuse.text: Don't call a broken printer 'top-notch'.
misuse.why: It means of the highest quality.

facts.def: Used when a picture or message matches your feeling.

example.text: That nap cat? Total mood.

misuse.text: Don't reply 'mood' to a friend's bad news.
misuse.why: It can sound lazy and dismissive.

facts.mean: Info that ruins a story's surprise.
facts.def: Secret details about a movie or show before you watch it.

example.text: No spoilers, please! I haven't finished it.

misuse.text: Don't shout 'spoiler' after saying the ending.

facts.def: Used to answer yes or say you're welcome.

example.text: Can you help me? You bet!

misuse.text: Don't say 'you bet' when you really can't.

facts.def: Used when someone suddenly becomes very angry.

example.text: Mom hit the roof when she saw the mess.

misuse.text: Don't say 'hit the roof' when mildly annoyed.

facts.def: A casual reply to thanks.

example.text: No problem, happy to help.

misuse.text: Don't say 'no problem' if it was hard.
misuse.why: It can hide your real effort.

facts.def: Used for something good that doesn't get enough credit.
facts.hook: Why doesn't anyone watch this show?

example.text: That show is so underrated.

misuse.text: Don't call a famous movie 'underrated'.
misuse.why: It means better than people think.

facts.def: Used to say something is pleasant or interesting.

example.text: That's a neat trick!

misuse.text: Don't call a friend's messy room 'neat'.
misuse.why: Neat means tidy or cool, so it confuses.

facts.mean: Be a big fan of someone.
facts.def: To support something very strongly.
facts.hook: I love this band so much!

example.text: I totally stan this band.

misuse.text: Don't say 'stan' about a casual preference.

facts.def: Used when something feels better or more emotional than usual.
facts.hook: Why is pizza better after soccer?

example.ctx: Eating with friends after a game
example.text: Pizza hits different after a long soccer game.

misuse.text: Don't say 'hits different' in a school essay.

facts.def: Someone or something that was first and respected.

example.text: He's the OG member of our club.

misuse.text: Don't call your new friend 'OG' on day one.

facts.def: Used to praise someone who did exactly what was needed, with style.

example.text: Pirate costume? She understood the assignment.

misuse.text: Don't say it when someone missed the task.

facts.def: Used to show surprise or say "obviously".

example.text: No kidding, it rained all week.

misuse.text: Don't say 'no kidding' to your teacher's lesson.

facts.mean: A post about someone without naming them.
facts.def: A hint-filled post about someone that doesn't use their name.
facts.hook: A post that's clearly about me?

example.text: That's a subtweet about our club.

misuse.text: Don't send a 'subtweet' about your boss.
misuse.why: People may figure out it's them.

facts.def: Used when you no longer care or enjoy something.
facts.hook: Everyone still talks about that trend!

example.text: That trend is old. I'm over it.

misuse.text: Don't say 'I'm over it' while still crying.
misuse.why: Your words and feelings won't match.

facts.def: To sense the mood and act wisely.

example.text: Read the room before telling that joke.

misuse.text: Don't tell someone to 'read the room' loudly.

facts.def: Used to show surprise or disbelief.

example.text: No way! You got tickets?

misuse.text: Don't say 'no way' when someone asks for help.
misuse.why: It sounds like a harsh refusal.

facts.def: Told to someone who spends too much time on the internet.

example.text: Touch grass, it's sunny out.

misuse.text: Don't tell someone sad to 'touch grass'.
misuse.why: It sounds dismissive of their feelings.

facts.def: Used when you are really enjoying something and want more.

example.text: They're singing my song. Living for it!

misuse.text: Don't say 'living for it' about a boring meeting.

facts.mean: Tease someone in a funny way.
facts.def: To joke about someone's flaws, often as a game.
facts.hook: My friends mocked my hat. Lovingly!

example.text: My friends roasted my hat.

misuse.text: Don't 'roast' your boss in a meeting.

facts.def: A reaction to something unlucky or embarrassing.
facts.hook: My test score was terrible. Help!

example.text: Oof, that test was tough!

misuse.text: Don't say 'oof' at a funeral.
misuse.why: It's too casual for deep sorrow.

facts.def: To post things to upset or tease others.
facts.hook: He posts silly comments to annoy!

example.text: Ignore him, he's just trolling.

misuse.text: Don't call someone a 'troll' for disagreeing politely.
misuse.why: It means purposely annoying, not honest.

facts.def: Used when you are losing control of your feelings.
facts.hook: Four kids, one phone, zero quiet!

example.text: I'm losing it with all this noise.

misuse.text: Don't tell your boss 'I'm losing it' casually.

facts.def: A casual goodbye when you will meet again some day.

example.text: Nice meeting you, see you around!

misuse.text: Don't say 'see you around' to set a meeting.
misuse.why: It's vague, with no fixed time.

facts.def: Used when something happens unexpectedly.

example.text: She called me out of the blue.

misuse.text: Don't say 'out of the blue' about expected news.

facts.def: To stop seeing someone's posts.

example.text: I unfollowed him after too many posts.

misuse.text: Don't announce you 'unfollowed' your friend publicly.

facts.def: Used to say something is true in a quiet, not obvious way.

example.text: I lowkey want to stay home and nap.

misuse.text: Don't say 'lowkey' about a huge, loud love.

facts.def: A close group of friends.

example.text: My squad is going bowling.

misuse.text: Don't call your coworkers your 'squad' in reports.
misuse.why: It's too casual for formal writing.

facts.mean: Very honest, in a cool way.
facts.def: Used for a reply or action that is fearless and a bit harsh.

example.text: That reply was savage, but funny.

misuse.text: Don't call your teacher's feedback 'savage'.

facts.def: To stop thinking about the past and continue.

example.text: Let's move on to the next game.

misuse.text: Don't tell someone to 'move on' after a loss.

facts.def: Used to tell someone to relax.

example.text: Take it easy this weekend.

misuse.text: Don't tell a panicking friend to 'take it easy'.
misuse.why: It sounds like you ignore the urgency.

facts.def: Used when you can't figure something out.

example.text: I'm scratching my head over this puzzle.

misuse.text: Don't say 'scratching my head' about an itchy scalp.

facts.def: Used when you love something very much.
facts.hook: I replayed this song twenty times!

example.text: I'm obsessed with this new song.

misuse.text: Don't tell a coworker you're 'obsessed' with her.
misuse.why: It can sound creepy, not friendly.

facts.mean: The extra person in a pair.
facts.def: A person who feels left out when two others are together.

example.text: I felt like a third wheel.

misuse.text: Don't say 'third wheel' about a car.
misuse.why: It means an extra person in a pair.

facts.def: A reaction to something impressive or surprising.

example.text: Sheesh, you finished that so fast!

misuse.text: Don't say 'sheesh' to your boss.

facts.def: Used when you feel the happiest you can.

example.text: She's on cloud nine after the news.

misuse.text: Don't say 'on cloud nine' about a cloudy day.

facts.def: A quick moment to see how someone feels or if a place feels good.

example.text: Quick vibe check: is this music okay?

misuse.text: Don't run a 'vibe check' on your teacher.

facts.def: Used when you are very shocked or upset by something.

example.text: I'm shook, I got a perfect score!

misuse.text: Don't say 'shook' after drinking a milkshake.

facts.def: Used when you are very, very pleased.

example.text: She was over the moon about the news.

misuse.text: Don't say 'over the moon' about space travel.

facts.def: Relaxing and enjoying the mood or music.

example.text: We're just vibing to music today.

misuse.text: Don't say 'vibing' about a vibrating phone.
misuse.why: It means enjoying a relaxed mood.

facts.mean: A look that says you are not sure.
facts.def: A look from the corner of your eye showing doubt.
facts.hook: She looked at me sideways. Why?

example.text: She gave me the side-eye.

misuse.text: Don't give your boss the 'side-eye'.

facts.def: Used when you feel excited and full of energy.
facts.hook: Concert tonight! Can you believe it?

example.text: I'm so pumped for the concert!

misuse.text: Don't say you're 'pumped' about a flat tire.

facts.def: A way to encourage someone.

example.text: Deep breath, you've got this!

misuse.text: Don't say 'you've got this' to someone failing badly.
misuse.why: It can sound false or mocking.

facts.def: Used to show you are pleased.

example.text: Sweet! We got front-row seats!

misuse.text: Don't say 'sweet' about sad news.

facts.def: Used when something stays in your thoughts all the time.

example.text: That silly song lives in my head rent-free.

misuse.text: Don't tell your landlord it lives 'rent-free'.

facts.def: Used when something is very funny.

example.text: That video is a riot!

misuse.text: Don't say 'a riot' about a serious speech.

facts.def: Used to say something made you laugh.

example.text: The puppy video is too funny.

misuse.text: Don't say 'too funny' to a sad person.

facts.def: Used when you're thrilled about something.
facts.hook: Road trip with my friends tomorrow!

example.text: I'm stoked about the trip!

misuse.text: Don't say 'stoked' in a formal speech.

facts.def: Used playfully for crazy but funny behavior.

example.text: My cat is unhinged at midnight.

misuse.text: Don't call your friend's mood 'unhinged' seriously.
misuse.why: It can sound like an insult.

facts.def: Used when something has made you angry.
facts.hook: My flight got delayed again. Ugh!

example.text: I'm ticked off about the delay.

misuse.text: Don't say 'ticked off' about a checklist.

facts.def: Used when you didn't understand or can't believe something.

example.text: Wait, what? The party is tomorrow?

misuse.text: Don't say 'wait, what' to your boss's order.

facts.mean: The feeling or mood of a place.
facts.def: The mood or feeling you get from a person, place or thing.

example.text: I love the vibe in this little café.

misuse.text: Don't say 'vibe' in a legal contract.

facts.mean: Throw something with a lot of energy.
facts.def: A playful word for throwing something away.

example.text: I yeeted my paper into the bin.

misuse.text: Don't 'yeet' fragile glass across the room.
